6.title: Create
6.content: Use PUT to submit a document. If no document exists for the UUID, it is created. If one already exists, it is replaced (see Replace). The submission is queued for processing and review, so it does not appear on ReliefWeb immediately. PUT https://api.reliefweb.int/v2/{reports|jobs|training}/{uuid}?appname=REPLACE-WITH-APP-NAME . Send headers X-RW-POST-API-KEY and X-RW-POST-API-PROVIDER. See Access and credentials.

7.title: Create a document
7.content: Generate the UUID from the document url first. See Trusted URLs and UUIDs. curl -X PUT "https://api.reliefweb.int/v2/reports/c27c51bd-e6b6-5c09-91fd-ef122afdde8e?appname=REPLACE-WITH-APP-NAME" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "X-RW-POST-API-KEY: YOUR-API-KEY" \ -H "X-RW-POST-API-PROVIDER: YOUR-PROVIDER-UUID" \ -d @report.json . Full payloads: Report examples, Job examples, Training examples.

8.title: Responses
8.content: . | Queued: 202 with “Document queued for processing.” | No changes: 200 with “No changes.” if the payload is identical to your previous submission. Nothing is queued again. | .

9.title: Errors
9.content: . | 400 if the payload is invalid. Check it against the schema for the document type. | 403 if the UUID belongs to a document created by another provider, or if your provider is not allowed to post this type of content. | 422 if the existing document is refused, duplicate, or for reports archive. These documents can no longer be changed. | . See Responses, limits, and errors for all error codes and rate limits.

10.title: Replace an existing document
10.content: If a document already exists for this UUID, the same PUT replaces it entirely. Use this when your system always has the full record and resends it. For targeted edits, use Update (PATCH) instead. | Send the complete document, including all required fields. | Omitted optional fields are cleared. For reports, this includes file: attachments missing from the map are removed. | A changed submission goes back through editorial review. | . Next: Update .

12.title: Who can publish
12.content: Organizations listed on reliefweb.int/organizations can use the Publish API once they have an approved appname and Publish access.

13.title: Request Publish access
13.content: Contact ReliefWeb and include: . | Organization name | Email of your ReliefWeb account | Document types you will publish (reports, jobs, training) | Trusted URL prefixes for documents, files, and images. If you host files on a separate CDN or storage domain, include both your organization’s domain (for permanent url identifiers) and the CDN prefix (for download_url). See Trusted URLs and UUIDs. | . After approval, ReliefWeb creates one API provider per document type you requested (with your organization and trusted URL prefixes) and grants the API User role to your ReliefWeb account, giving you access to your API Dashboard (see below).

14.title: API Dashboard
14.content: Open the API Dashboard on reliefweb.int to find each provider’s UUID and generate an API key. Use the matching provider UUID when you call that document type’s endpoint.

15.title: Changes after approval
15.content: Contact ReliefWeb if you need to: . | Update trusted URL prefixes | Add another document type (a new provider) | Link another ReliefWeb account to your providers | .

16.title: Authentication
16.content: Every request to the Publish API must include: . | Credential | Where | Name | . | Appname | Query parameter | appname | . | API key | Header | X-RW-POST-API-KEY | . | Provider ID (UUID) | Header | X-RW-POST-API-PROVIDER | . appname is the same value used for Read / search. Keep the API key secret.

17.title: Call the API
17.content: curl -X PUT "https://api.reliefweb.int/v2/reports/YOUR-DOCUMENT-UUID?appname=REPLACE-WITH-APP-NAME" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "X-RW-POST-API-KEY: YOUR-API-KEY" \ -H "X-RW-POST-API-PROVIDER: YOUR-PROVIDER-UUID" \ -d @payload.json . DELETE uses the same URL shape and headers, with no request body. See Withdraw. Next: Trusted URLs and UUIDs .

30.content: | Issue | Likely cause | What to do | . | Invalid taxonomy / unknown id | Wrong integer, name/ISO3 sent instead of id, or stale id | Look up the term via /v2/sources, /v2/countries, or /v2/references/... and send the integer id in an array | . | Missing required field | Required property omitted or set to null | Include every required field from Job fields; required fields cannot be cleared on PATCH | . | UUID / url mismatch | uuid not derived from the exact url string | Recompute uuid5(ReliefWeb namespace, url); see Trusted URLs and UUIDs | . | Trusted URL rejected | url (or other URL fields) outside approved prefixes | Use a URL under your trusted document prefix; request prefix updates via credentials | . | Invalid JSON / schema errors | Malformed JSON, wrong types (string instead of array of ints), title too short, empty body | Validate against the job schema; check min lengths and maxItems | . | how_to_apply / body rejected | Control characters, leading/trailing spaces, or too short | Use markdown/HTML within the allowlist; keep length ≥ 10; avoid odd whitespace | . See also Responses, limits, and errors.

31.title: Report examples
31.content: Replace the example IDs and URLs with your own. A successful create typically returns HTTP 202. Field rules: Report fields. Attachment deep dive: Files and images.

32.title: Minimal valid report
32.content: Required fields only (text body, no PDF or image). curl -X PUT "https://api.reliefweb.int/v2/reports/c27c51bd-e6b6-5c09-91fd-ef122afdde8e?appname=REPLACE-WITH-APP-NAME" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "X-RW-POST-API-KEY: YOUR-API-KEY" \ -H "X-RW-POST-API-PROVIDER: YOUR-PROVIDER-UUID" \ -d @report.json . { "url": "https://myorganization.org/report/12345", "uuid": "c27c51bd-e6b6-5c09-91fd-ef122afdde8e", "title": "Example situation report for Country X", "source": [1503], "country": [13], "format": [10], "language": [267], "published": "2024-06-06T01:00:00+00:00", "body": "Short overview or full article text in markdown or HTML." } .

34.content: | Field | Id | Meaning | Look it up | . | source | 1503 | UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs | GET /v2/sources/1503 | . | country | 13 | Afghanistan | GET /v2/countries/13 | . | format | 10 | Situation Report | GET /v2/references/content-formats/10 | . | language | 267 | English | GET /v2/references/languages/267 | . | theme | 4587 | (theme term — confirm via lookup) | GET /v2/references/themes/4587 | . Search countries by name or ISO3, then use the integer id in the payload (not the ISO3 code). The first country id is the primary country. GET https://api.reliefweb.int/v2/countries?appname=REPLACE-WITH-APP-NAME&query[value]=afghanistan . Example response (abbreviated): . { "totalCount": 1, "count": 1, "data": [ { "id": 13, "fields": { "name": "Afghanistan", "iso3": "AFG" } } ] } . Take id from the response and send "country": [13]. 35.title: Troubleshooting
35.content: | Issue | Likely cause | What to do | . | Invalid taxonomy / unknown id | Wrong integer, name/ISO3 instead of id | Look up via /v2/sources, /v2/countries, /v2/disasters, or /v2/references/... | . | Missing required field | Required property omitted | Include every required field from Report fields | . | UUID / url mismatch | Document or file UUID not derived from the exact url | Recompute UUID v5; see Trusted URLs and UUIDs | . | Trusted URL rejected | Document, file, or image URL outside approved prefixes | Register document/file/image prefixes; see credentials | . | file shape errors | Sent as a JSON array, or map key ≠ attachment uuid | Send a UUID-keyed object; key must match uuid and uuid5(document_uuid, file.url) | . | Checksum / download failures | Wrong SHA-256, unreachable download_url, or non-PDF | Recompute checksum of the bytes at download_url; ensure PDF ≤ 20MB | . | Image rejected | Missing fields, wrong extension, or too small | Require download_url, checksum, description, copyright; .jpg/.png/.webp; min width 700px | . | Invalid JSON / schema errors | Wrong types or short strings | Validate against the report schema | . See also Responses, limits, and errors.

36.title: Break down results
36.content: Get counts broken down by a field, for example how many jobs per country. In the API these are facets. Set "limit": 0 on the main request when you only need facets, not result rows. For a single total of all matches (totalCount), see Sort and paginate.

37.title: Parameter specification
37.content: facets is an array of objects. Keys per facet: . | Key | Type | Meaning | . | field | string | Date, category, or status field; see Resources | . | name | string | Label when faceting the same field more than once | . | limit | integer | Terms to return for non-date facets (default 10) | . | sort | string | {type}:{direction} where type is count or value, direction asc or desc (default count:desc) | . | filter | object | Extra filter applied only to this facet | . | interval | string | For dates: year, month, week, or day | . | scope | string | default (after global query+filter), query (ignore global filter), or global (ignore both) | .

38.title: Top countries for jobs
38.content: Count jobs by country (top 20); omit result rows (limit: 0): . POST . https://api.reliefweb.int/v2/jobs?appname=REPLACE-WITH-APP-NAME . { "limit": 0, "facets": [ { "field": "country", "limit": 20 } ] } . Example response (abbreviated): . { "totalCount": 15234, "count": 0, "data": [], "embedded": { "facets": { "country": { "data": [ { "value": "South Sudan", "count": 412 }, { "value": "Yemen", "count": 387 }, { "value": "Syrian Arab Republic", "count": 301 } ], "missing": 12, "type": "term" } } } } .

39.title: Sort facet terms
39.content: Count reports by country, rarest (smallest counts) first (10 terms): . POST . https://api.reliefweb.int/v2/reports?appname=REPLACE-WITH-APP-NAME . { "limit": 0, "facets": [ { "field": "country", "sort": "count:asc", "limit": 10 } ] } .

40.title: Date intervals
40.content: Facet limit does not apply to date intervals. Restrict with a facet filter if needed. Count reports by year created: . POST . https://api.reliefweb.int/v2/reports?appname=REPLACE-WITH-APP-NAME . { "limit": 0, "facets": [ { "field": "date.created", "interval": "year" } ] } . Count reports by month created in 2025: . POST . https://api.reliefweb.int/v2/reports?appname=REPLACE-WITH-APP-NAME . { "limit": 0, "facets": [ { "field": "date.created", "interval": "month", "filter": { "field": "date.created", "value": { "from": "2025-01-01T00:00:00+00:00", "to": "2025-12-31T23:59:59+00:00" } } } ] } .

41.title: Scope
41.content: Use scope when a global query or filter should not apply to a facet: . | default: after global query and filter | query: ignore global filter | global: ignore global query and filter | . Name facets with name when faceting the same field more than once or comparing scopes side by side. Next: Get one item .

42.title: FAQ
42.content: Common questions. For walkthroughs, start with Read / search or Publish. Suggestions welcome via contact.

43.title: General
43.content: Are client libraries available? . Yes. There are simple clients for PHP and Golang.

44.title: Read / search
44.content: How often is the data updated? . In real time. Content is available whenever it is added or updated on ReliefWeb. How far does the data go back? . Reports have been posted continuously since 1996 (ReliefWeb launch). UN reports on major disasters from the 1980s are also available. Jobs started in 2001 and training in 1998, with API data available from 2011 onwards. Why are my results almost empty? . On /v2/{resource} the default profile is minimal (title or name only). Set "profile": "list" for a practical browsing set, or full for everything. Single-record requests (/v2/{resource}/{id}) default to profile=default. See Choose fields and Resources for details. Why don’t I see expired or archived items? . Default presets hide archived disasters and expired jobs/training. Use "preset": "analysis" when you need historical content. See Default filters (preset). How can I get exact results for my search terms? . | Filters: quote the value and/or use a field marked exact under Resources. Examples: Filter. | Full-text query: phrases, booleans, and field prefixes are covered in Search. | . How can I get just the total? . Each response includes totalCount (all matches), separate from count (items on this page). Set "limit": 0 when you only need the total. See Sort and paginate.

45.title: Publish
45.content: What’s the difference between url and download_url? . On report attachments, url is the permanent attachment identifier on your organization domain. download_url is the public URL where ReliefWeb downloads the file (your site or a CDN). See Trusted URLs and UUIDs. Why did I get HTTP 202 instead of 200? . 202 means the document was queued for processing. That is the usual success for creates, replaces, and updates. See Responses, limits, and errors. When should I use PUT, PATCH, or DELETE? . | Want to… | Use | . | Create or replace entirely | PUT — Create | . | Change some fields | PATCH — Update | . | Withdraw | DELETE — Withdraw | .

47.title: Choose fields
47.content: Two parameters control which fields appear in each result: . | Parameter | Role | . | profile | Default set of fields in each result | . | fields | Include or exclude specific fields on top of the profile | . For default status filters and list-oriented sort, see preset.

48.title: Profiles (profile)
48.content: Requests to /v2/{resource} default to profile=minimal (title or name only). Single-record requests (/v2/{resource}/{id}) default to profile=default (nearly all fields; see below). Override with the profile string, or refine further with fields. | Profile | When to use | What you get | . | minimal | Compact results, lookups by title/name | Title or name only (default on /v2/{resource}) | . | list | Browsable result sets | Listing-oriented fields (as on ReliefWeb listing pages). Exact set varies by resource | . | full | Complete payloads | All fields for the resource | . | default | Single-record fetches | All fields for most resources (default on /v2/{resource}/{id}) | . | suggest | Typeahead UIs | Compact name fields for countries, disasters, sources, and references | . Most examples use "profile": "list". For the exact field sets and preset status / sort / query defaults, open the resource page’s Defaults tables under Resources. List countries with the list profile and include each iso3 code: . POST . https://api.reliefweb.int/v2/countries?appname=REPLACE-WITH-APP-NAME . { "profile": "list", "fields": { "include": ["iso3"] }, "limit": 5 } .

49.title: Fields (fields)
49.content: fields is an object with two optional arrays: . | Key | Type | Meaning | . | include | array of strings | Extra fields to add beyond the profile | . | exclude | array of strings | Fields to remove from the profile | . List reports with list fields plus format.name: . POST . https://api.reliefweb.int/v2/reports?appname=REPLACE-WITH-APP-NAME . { "limit": 3, "profile": "list", "fields": { "include": ["format.name"] } } . List full reports but omit body and body-html: . POST . https://api.reliefweb.int/v2/reports?appname=REPLACE-WITH-APP-NAME . { "limit": 3, "profile": "full", "fields": { "exclude": ["body", "body-html"] } } . Available field names for each resource are listed under Resources. Next: Sort and paginate .

50.title: Training fields
50.content: How to populate each training field. Taxonomy and source values are ReliefWeb integer ids. Document url and uuid follow Trusted URLs and UUIDs. See conditional fields on the Training hub for country and fee_information. Canonical schema: training.json.

51.title: url
51.content: | Required | yes | . | Type | string (IRI / URL) | . | Identifier | Trusted URL / IRI | . Immutable unique identifier in URL form under your trusted document prefix. Used to generate the training UUID. Does not need to resolve to a live page. Never change after first submission. Example . "https://myorganization.org/training/12345" . Validation . | Must start with a trusted document prefix . | Max length 2048 . | Never change after the first successful submission . | . See also . | Trusted URLs and UUIDs | .

52.title: uuid
52.content: | Required | yes | . | Type | string (UUID v5) | . | Identifier | UUID v5 | . Training UUID v5 computed as uuid5(ReliefWeb namespace, url). Must match what the server computes from the exact url string. Example . "c2484d60-fa5d-591e-bcdd-401ffa63b92c" . Validation . | Must be UUID format . | Must equal uuid5('8e27a998-c362-5d1f-b152-d474e1d36af2', url) . | Rejected if it does not match the server computation . | . See also . | Trusted URLs and UUIDs | .

53.title: title
53.content: | Required | yes | . | Type | string | . Training title only. Do not put location, date, or organization name in this field. Example . "Example Introduction to Humanitarian Response" . Validation . | Length 10–255 characters . | Must contain letters . | No leading, trailing, or consecutive spaces . | .

54.title: source
54.content: | Required | yes | . | Type | array of integer | . | Identifier | ReliefWeb integer taxonomy ID (not a UUID) | . | Lookup | /v2/sources — see docs | . Source organization ID(s) from /v2/sources (ReliefWeb integer taxonomy IDs, not UUIDs). Example . [1503] . Validation . | 1–30 unique integer IDs . | Each value must be a valid /v2/sources id . | .

55.title: format
55.content: | Required | yes | . | Type | array of integer | . | Identifier | ReliefWeb integer taxonomy ID (not a UUID) | . | Lookup | /v2/references/training-formats — see docs | . Training-format ID(s) from /v2/references/training-formats (on-site and/or online). On-site id is 4606; online is 4607. Example . [4607] . Validation . | 1–2 unique integer IDs . | Must be valid training-formats reference ids . | .

56.title: country
56.content: | Required | conditional — Required when format includes on-site (id 4606); omit (do not send) otherwise | . | Type | array of integer | . | Identifier | ReliefWeb integer taxonomy ID (not a UUID) | . | Lookup | /v2/countries — see docs | . Country ID(s) from /v2/countries. Mandatory when format includes on-site; otherwise the property is not allowed. Example . [13] . 100.title: Files and images
100.content: Only reports support PDF attachments and an optional cover image. Jobs and training do not. Field summaries: Report fields. Full payloads: Report examples. In the Publish API, file is a map keyed by permanent file UUID, not a JSON array. How url, download_url, and file UUIDs relate is explained in Trusted URLs and UUIDs.

101.title: Attachment fields
101.content: | Field | Required | Meaning | . | Map key / uuid | Yes | Permanent file UUID = uuid5(document_uuid, url) | . | url | Yes (when creating) | Permanent attachment identifier under your organization’s domain. Do not use a variable CDN or versioned URL. Optional on later submissions if unchanged. Keep it the same to publish a new version of the file. | . | download_url | Yes | Public URL ReliefWeb downloads. May equal url, or point to a CDN/storage host registered in your trusted file prefixes. Changing it does not change the UUID. | . | filename | Yes | Must end in lowercase .pdf | . | checksum | Yes | Lowercase SHA-256 of the file at download_url | . | description | No | On PATCH, omit to keep; null to clear | . | language | No | Optional ISO code: ar, en, es, fr, ru, zh, or ot. On PATCH, omit to keep; null to clear | . Optional root field file_order: an array of attachment UUIDs that sets display order. Examples below use the same IDs as Trusted URLs and UUIDs: . | Document: c27c51bd-e6b6-5c09-91fd-ef122afdde8e | File: 78d63e84-e2b4-5467-813d-1c2456f40d63 | .

102.title: Checksum
102.content: checksum is the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the file at download_url: . # macOS shasum -a 256 path/to/file.pdf | awk '{print tolower($1)}' # Linux sha256sum path/to/file.pdf | awk '{print tolower($1)}' .

103.title: Publish a new version of a file
103.content: This is the recommended way to update a PDF. Keep the attachment’s permanent url and uuid the same, and change only download_url and checksum. Everyone who already has a link to the file on ReliefWeb then gets the new version. The description and language are kept unless you send new values. Do not add the new version under a new url. That creates a separate attachment with a new UUID. Depending on the method, the old file is either still listed next to the new one (PATCH) or removed (PUT), and existing links to it never reach the new version. | Keep the same map key, uuid, and permanent url (your organization domain, not a CDN path). | Point download_url at the new file. It can stay the same if you overwrote the file at that location. | Send the new checksum. ReliefWeb uses it to detect that the content changed. If the checksum is unchanged, the file is not downloaded again. | Use PATCH so the other attachments stay untouched. | . In the example below, only download_url and checksum change. curl -X PATCH "https://api.reliefweb.int/v2/reports/c27c51bd-e6b6-5c09-91fd-ef122afdde8e?appname=REPLACE-WITH-APP-NAME" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "X-RW-POST-API-KEY: YOUR-API-KEY" \ -H "X-RW-POST-API-PROVIDER: YOUR-PROVIDER-UUID" \ -d @replace-file.json . { "file": { "78d63e84-e2b4-5467-813d-1c2456f40d63": { "uuid": "78d63e84-e2b4-5467-813d-1c2456f40d63", "url": "https://myorganization.org/report/12345/attachment.pdf", "download_url": "https://cdn.example.org/files/2026-06/sitrep-v2.pdf", "filename": "attachment.pdf", "checksum": "46e71dcadaee27ff9248490c5310bd2f9a04da602638b1f1d71bb01cdfaaf9a0" } } } .

104.title: Add an attachment
104.content: Send a PATCH with a new UUID key. Other files are kept. { "file": { "0c478b4a-6c1a-5153-bd73-96fecb1bd49c": { "uuid": "0c478b4a-6c1a-5153-bd73-96fecb1bd49c", "url": "https://myorganization.org/report/12345/annex.pdf", "download_url": "https://myorganization.org/report/12345/annex.pdf", "filename": "annex.pdf", "checksum": "ecf9d6481917f47bbcb47c4ba934a14177cb919c2c597444b9a764073f827980", "description": "Annex", "language": "en" } } } . Generate the new UUID with uuid5(document_uuid, url). See Trusted URLs and UUIDs.

105.title: Remove one attachment
105.content: Send a PATCH that sets that UUID to null. Other files stay. { "file": { "0c478b4a-6c1a-5153-bd73-96fecb1bd49c": null } } .

106.title: Remove all attachments
106.content: { "file": null } . On PUT, an empty object {} also clears all attachments. On PATCH, {} means “change nothing about files.” .

107.title: Reorder attachments
107.content: Send file_order without changing file: . { "file_order": [ "78d63e84-e2b4-5467-813d-1c2456f40d63", "0c478b4a-6c1a-5153-bd73-96fecb1bd49c" ] } . Listed UUIDs come first in that order. Any unlisted attachments keep their relative order at the end. Unknown ids are ignored.

108.title: Full replace of the attachment set
108.content: Use PUT with a complete document payload whose file map lists exactly the attachments that should remain. Anything absent from the map is removed. See Replace. Full create-with-PDF examples: Report examples.

109.title: Set or clear the cover image
109.content: image is a single object that you replace as a whole. Required fields: download_url, checksum, description, copyright. Do not send a client uuid. Set or replace: . { "image": { "download_url": "https://myorganization.org/images/report-12345.png", "checksum": "c24863f6aa2065dd5071a831ee78439260ea72983799dd3e88fbfb4aa08fdc18", "description": "Test image", "copyright": "Test NGO" } } . Clear: . { "image": null } . Next: Jobs .

110.title: Filter
110.content: Use filter to restrict which items are returned. Simple filters use field and value. Complex ones nest conditions with AND / OR.

111.title: Parameter specification
111.content: filter is an object with these keys: . | Key | Type | Meaning | . | field | string | Field to filter on; see Resources | . | value | boolean, integer, string, array, or object | Match value(s). For dates/numbers, use { "from", "to" } (open-ended if only one bound). Omit value to test whether the field exists. | . | operator | string | AND or OR when combining array values or conditions | . | negate | boolean | When true, select items that do not match | . | conditions | array | Nest multiple filters | .

112.title: Filter by country
112.content: Return reports whose primary country is South Sudan (SSD): . POST . https://api.reliefweb.int/v2/reports?appname=REPLACE-WITH-APP-NAME . { "filter": { "field": "primary_country.iso3", "value": "SSD" }, "profile": "list", "limit": 5 } . You can also filter on country.id, country.name, or primary_country.name. Discover IDs via /v2/countries or references.

113.title: Exact phrase matching
113.content: Filtering on a name field without quotes can match tokens separately. Quote the value and/or use a field marked exact in Resources. Find the disaster named exactly Myanmar: Earthquake: . POST . https://api.reliefweb.int/v2/disasters?appname=REPLACE-WITH-APP-NAME . { "filter": { "field": "name", "value": "\"Myanmar: Earthquake\"" }, "profile": "list", "limit": 5 } .

114.title: Date range
114.content: Return reports created in 2024: . POST . https://api.reliefweb.int/v2/reports?appname=REPLACE-WITH-APP-NAME . { "filter": { "field": "date.created", "value": { "from": "2024-01-01T00:00:00+00:00", "to": "2024-12-31T23:59:59+00:00" } }, "profile": "list", "limit": 5 } . Use ISO 8601 dates. In GET URLs, encode + as %2B.

115.title: Combined conditions
115.content: Return Health-themed reports for Syria (SYR): . POST . https://api.reliefweb.int/v2/reports?appname=REPLACE-WITH-APP-NAME . { "filter": { "operator": "AND", "conditions": [ { "field": "primary_country.iso3", "value": "SYR" }, { "field": "theme", "value": "Health" } ] }, "profile": "list", "limit": 5 } .

116.title: Field exists
116.content: Omit value to select items where the field is present. Return reports that have a headline: . POST . https://api.reliefweb.int/v2/reports?appname=REPLACE-WITH-APP-NAME . { "filter": { "field": "headline" }, "profile": "list", "limit": 5 } .

117.title: Negate
117.content: Return reports tagged France or Spain, but not Italy: . POST . https://api.reliefweb.int/v2/reports?appname=REPLACE-WITH-APP-NAME . { "filter": { "operator": "AND", "conditions": [ { "field": "country", "value": ["France", "Spain"], "operator": "OR" }, { "field": "country", "value": "Italy", "negate": true } ] }, "profile": "list", "limit": 5 } .

118.title: Default filters (preset)
118.content: preset is a string. It applies bundled status filters and related defaults so you get the usual public listing behaviour without writing those filters by hand. It does not choose which fields appear in each result. That is profile and fields. Exact status filters differ by resource. See each resource’s Defaults section under Resources. | Preset | Use | . | minimal | Default sensible status filters for most requests (hides expired jobs/training and archived disasters) | . | latest | List-oriented sort (typically by date; countries and sources by id) | . | analysis | Include archived disasters and expired jobs/training for historical analysis | . Include expired jobs for trends: . POST . https://api.reliefweb.int/v2/jobs?appname=REPLACE-WITH-APP-NAME . { "preset": "analysis", "profile": "list", "limit": 5 } . Search for nutrition reports, newest first: . POST . https://api.reliefweb.int/v2/reports?appname=REPLACE-WITH-APP-NAME . { "preset": "latest", "query": { "value": "nutrition" }, "profile": "list", "limit": 5 } . With preset: "latest" and a query, results are sorted by date. With the default minimal preset and a query, results are typically ordered by relevance unless you set sort yourself. Next: Choose fields .

119.title: Get one item
119.content: Fetch a single document by ReliefWeb id or UUID: . GET /v2/{resource}/{id|uuid} . Single-record requests are GET (or HEAD) only. Allowed parameters: profile, fields, preset, and slim. Defaults are preset=minimal and profile=default. If the item is excluded by the preset (for example an expired job or archived disaster under minimal), the API returns 404. Pass preset=analysis on the query string to fetch historical items. Fetch report 1082221 with the full profile: . GET . https://api.reliefweb.int/v2/reports/1082221?appname=REPLACE-WITH-APP-NAME&profile=full . Example response (abbreviated): . { "href": "https://api.reliefweb.int/v2/reports/1082221?appname=REPLACE-WITH-APP-NAME&profile=full", "time": 8, "totalCount": 1, "count": 1, "data": [ { "id": 1082221, "score": 1, "href": "https://api.reliefweb.int/v2/reports/1082221", "fields": { "title": "Example situation report for Country X", "url": "https://reliefweb.int/node/1082221", "date": { "created": "2024-06-06T01:00:00+00:00", "original": "2024-06-05T00:00:00+00:00" }, "source": [ { "name": "Example Organization", "shortname": "EO" } ] } } ] } . Fetch the same report with list fields plus source.name and body: . GET . https://api.reliefweb.int/v2/reports/1082221?appname=REPLACE-WITH-APP-NAME&profile=list&fields[include][]=source.name&fields[include][]=body .

120.title: From search results to full item
120.content: . | List with profile: "list" to browse. | Read data[].id, data[].fields.uuid (when included), or data[].href. | Request the item with profile=full for detail. | . On the website, many items are also at https://reliefweb.int/node/{id}. Next: GET vs POST .

121.title: GET vs POST
121.content: Search endpoints (/v2/reports, /v2/jobs, …) accept GET or POST with the same parameters. With GET, put them on the query string; with POST, put them in a JSON body. Always pass appname as a URL query parameter, including for POST. Do not put it in the JSON body. Use POST when the request includes nested structures (query, filter, facets, fields). The JSON body stays readable.

122.title: Same request, two forms
122.content: Search for drought reports in Ethiopia (ETH) as JSON POST: . POST . https://api.reliefweb.int/v2/reports?appname=REPLACE-WITH-APP-NAME . { "query": { "value": "drought" }, "filter": { "field": "primary_country.iso3", "value": "ETH" }, "limit": 3, "profile": "list" } . Same request as a GET query string: . GET . https://api.reliefweb.int/v2/reports?appname=REPLACE-WITH-APP-NAME&query[value]=drought&filter[field]=primary_country.iso3&filter[value]=ETH&limit=3&profile=list .

123.title: Encoding tips
123.content: . | Arrays: fields[include][]=title&fields[include][]=body | Nested objects: filter[value][from]=...&filter[value][to]=... | Facet list indexes: facets[0][field]=country&facets[0][limit]=20 | Encode + in timezone offsets as %2B | Keep URLs reasonably short. Large filters belong in POST bodies. | .

136.content: The ReliefWeb API gives you programmatic access to humanitarian reports, disasters, jobs, training, and related data as JSON over HTTPS.

138.title: Appname
138.content: Every API URL needs a pre-approved appname so ReliefWeb can monitor usage. Pass it as a query parameter on the URL (including for POST, PATCH, or DELETE requests): . https://api.reliefweb.int/v2/reports?appname=YOUR-APPROVED-APPNAME . Request one with this short form. Use a combination of your organization name, purpose, and random characters. ReliefWeb reviews requests and replies by email. Examples in this documentation use REPLACE-WITH-APP-NAME. 140.content: Anyone may use the ReliefWeb API. Reports, jobs, and training may include material owned by the original source. Respect those rights when reusing content. ReliefWeb may log calls and analyze usage. Always send a valid appname so usage can be attributed.

147.title: Responses, limits, and errors
147.content: All Publish API calls use the same path and authentication: . https://api.reliefweb.int/v2/{reports|jobs|training}/{uuid}?appname=REPLACE-WITH-APP-NAME . Send headers X-RW-POST-API-KEY and X-RW-POST-API-PROVIDER. See Access and credentials. How-to pages: Create · Update · Withdraw. Responses are short JSON-encoded strings (for example "Document queued for processing.") with an HTTP status code.

148.title: Rules that apply to all methods
148.content: | Rule | What it means | . | Same provider | You can only change documents your provider created. The wrong provider returns 403. | . | Terminal statuses | Documents marked refused, duplicate, or (for reports) archive cannot be changed with PUT or PATCH (422). | . | No changes | If the payload is identical to the previous submission, you get 200 “No changes.” and nothing is re-queued. Exception: for withdrawn documents (and expired jobs/training), the same payload is accepted again so you can reopen. See also Replace. | . | Queue | If a document is still queued, a later submission for the same UUID replaces the queued item. | . | Rate limits | See Limits below. | .

149.title: Success responses
149.content: | HTTP | Message (typical) | Meaning | . | 202 | Document queued for processing. | Accepted and queued for import/review. | . | 200 | Document processed. | Processed without queuing (when applicable). | . | 200 | No changes. | Payload matches the last submission. Nothing is re-queued. | . | 200 | Document withdrawn. | DELETE succeeded. | . | 200 | Document already withdrawn. | DELETE when already withdrawn (safe to retry). | . | 200 | Document is already publicly unavailable (marked as refused). | DELETE on a terminal status (refused, duplicate, or for reports archive). The status is not changed. | . Most creates, replaces, and updates return 202.

151.content: Typical defaults (ReliefWeb may set different values for your provider): . | Limit | Typical value | . | Documents per day | 50 | . | Minimum interval | 1 document per minute | . 158.title: Reports
158.content: Submit a report for editorial review. PUT|PATCH|DELETE https://api.reliefweb.int/v2/reports/{uuid}?appname=REPLACE-WITH-APP-NAME . You need Access and credentials and Trusted URLs and UUIDs. For changes and withdrawals, see Update and Withdraw.

159.title: Field summary
159.content: Canonical schema: report.json. Field-by-field rules and examples: field reference. | Name | Required | Type | Description | . | url | yes | string (IRI / URL) | Immutable unique identifier in URL form under your trusted document prefix. Used to generate the document UUID. Does not need to resolve to a live page. Never change it after first submission. | . | uuid | yes | string (UUID v5) | Document UUID v5 computed as `uuid5(ReliefWeb namespace, url)`. Must match what the server computes from the exact url string. | . | title | yes | string | Original title of the article or file. For series, add date or other distinguishing details as needed. | . | source | yes | array of integer | Source organization ID(s) from /v2/sources (ReliefWeb integer taxonomy IDs, not UUIDs). | . | country | yes | array of integer | Country ID(s) from /v2/countries. The first entry is the primary country. Tag only the most relevant. | . | format | yes | array of integer | Single content-format ID from /v2/references/content-formats. | . | language | yes | array of integer | Language ID(s) from /v2/references/languages. If an attachment is not in an official UN language, mention that in the attachment description. | . | published | yes | string (date-time) | Original publication date-time (ISO 8601) of the document. | . | body | yes | string (markdown or HTML) | Full article text, or an executive summary when the main content is a PDF attachment. Markdown or a small set of HTML tags. | . | embargoed | no | string (date-time) | UTC/GMT date-time until which the document stays embargoed; it publishes automatically at that time. | . | origin | no | string (IRI / URL) | Optional real public page where readers can view the document. Unlike url, this should resolve to a live page. | . | file | no | object (UUID-keyed map) | PDF attachments keyed by permanent file UUID (max 10, 20MB each). Each value needs `uuid`, `download_url`, `filename`, `checksum`; `url` required on create. Use your organization domain for `url`; `download_url` may use a CDN. On `PUT`, the map replaces the whole attachment set; on `PATCH`, keys merge (`null` deletes that attachment). | . | file_order | no | array of UUID | Optional display order of attachment UUIDs. Unlisted attachments keep relative order at the end; unknown ids are ignored. | . | image | no | object | Cover or illustration image. Required properties: `download_url`, `checksum`, `description`, `copyright`. No client-supplied `uuid`. Sending an `image` object replaces the whole cover; on `PATCH`, send `"image": null` to remove it. | . | disaster | no | array of integer | Disaster ID(s) from /v2/disasters. Tag only the most relevant. | . | disaster_type | no | array of integer | Disaster-type ID(s) from /v2/references/disaster-types. Tag only the most relevant. | . | theme | no | array of integer | Theme ID(s) from /v2/references/themes. Tag only the most relevant. | . | notify | no | array of string (email) | Email addresses to notify when the document is published. | . Use integer ids for taxonomies (source, country, format, language, and optional tags) — not UUIDs. Resolve them with the read API and /v2/references.

160.content: . | Put the full article in body, or an executive summary when the main content is a PDF. | PDFs go in file (map of attachments, .pdf filename, max 20MB each, max 10). | An optional cover or illustration goes in image (.jpg / .png / .webp, min width 700px, max 5MB). | . Prefer PATCH for targeted field or attachment edits. Use PUT when you resend the full record from your system. See Update and Replace. | Goal | See | . | Rules, examples, and lookups for each field | Report fields | . | Minimal and production-style payloads, troubleshooting | Report examples | . | PDF and image details | Files and images | . | Change title or body only | Update | . | New PDF version, same permanent URL | Publish a new version of a file | . | Withdraw | Withdraw | . 166.title: Search
166.content: Use query for full-text search across a resource.

167.title: Parameter specification
167.content: query is an object with these keys: . | Key | Type | Meaning | . | value | string | Search string (required). Supports the syntax below. | . | fields | array | Optional list of fields to search (defaults depend on the resource) | . | operator | string | How spaces in value combine: AND or OR (default OR) | .

168.title: Basic search
168.content: Search for reports that mention cholera: . POST . https://api.reliefweb.int/v2/reports?appname=REPLACE-WITH-APP-NAME . { "query": { "value": "cholera" }, "profile": "list", "limit": 5, "sort": ["date:desc"] } . Search for reports whose title contains both flash and appeal: . POST . https://api.reliefweb.int/v2/reports?appname=REPLACE-WITH-APP-NAME . { "query": { "value": "flash appeal", "fields": ["title"], "operator": "AND" }, "profile": "list", "limit": 5 } .

169.title: Query string syntax
169.content: The query.value string supports phrases, field prefixes, booleans, wildcards, ranges, and boosting (similar to Elasticsearch query_string syntax). Phrases and proximity . "climate change" "food security crisis"~3 title:"flash appeal"~2 . Content inside valid double quotes is preserved, including special characters. Field queries . title:humanitarian country:Syria date:[2024-01-01 TO 2024-12-31] _exists_:file.url . Unknown field names are ignored (the colon is treated as a space). Fuzzy and wildcards . humanitarin~ climat* change earth?uake title:report* . Avoid wildcards on date fields. Ranges . Inclusive [min TO max], exclusive {min TO max}, and mixed brackets: . date:[2024-01-01 TO 2024-12-31] population:[1000000 TO *] age:>=10 date:>2024-01-01 . Boolean operators . AND, OR, NOT (also &&, ||, !). Prefix + (must) and - (must not) when they start a term: . (Syria OR Yemen) AND crisis title:test +required -excluded drought AND food security OR famine . Boosting . crisis^3 humanitarian title:"situation report"^2 OR sitrep . Grouping . title:(natural disaster) AND (country:Philippines OR country:Indonesia) . Example API call . Search for reports about cholera or "acute watery diarrhoea" in Yemen: . POST . https://api.reliefweb.int/v2/reports?appname=REPLACE-WITH-APP-NAME . { "query": { "value": "(cholera OR \"acute watery diarrhoea\") AND country:Yemen", "operator": "AND" }, "profile": "list", "limit": 5 } . Tips . | Use field names from Resources. | Quote phrases that contain special characters. | Close quotes and parentheses deliberately. The parser is lenient, but well-formed queries are more predictable. | Fields marked exact support a .exact suffix (for example source.shortname.exact). For exact matching with filters, see Filter. | . Next: Filter .

170.title: Sort and paginate
170.content: Use sort, limit, and offset to order results and page through large sets.

171.title: Parameter specification
171.content: | Parameter | Type | Meaning | . | sort | array of strings | Sortable fields and direction as field:asc or field:desc. Array order is priority. | . | limit | integer | Items to return (0–1000, default 10). Use 0 for counts/facets only. | . | offset | integer | Matching items to skip (default 0) | . In the response: . | count: items returned on this page | totalCount: all matches for the query/filter | . Set "limit": 0 when you only need totalCount or facets.

172.title: Sort
172.content: When a query is present and you omit sort, results are typically ordered by relevance (score:desc). Prefer an explicit, stable sort when paginating so pages do not drift as new content arrives. For the most recent results, use the latest preset or set sort yourself. List reports newest first, then by title: . POST . https://api.reliefweb.int/v2/reports?appname=REPLACE-WITH-APP-NAME . { "sort": ["date:desc", "title:asc"], "profile": "list", "limit": 5 } .

173.title: Paginate
173.content: First page of Ethiopia (ETH) reports (10 per page): . POST . https://api.reliefweb.int/v2/reports?appname=REPLACE-WITH-APP-NAME . { "filter": { "field": "primary_country.iso3", "value": "ETH" }, "profile": "list", "limit": 10, "offset": 0, "sort": ["date:desc"] } . Next page: same request with "offset": 10, then 20, and so on, until offset + count >= totalCount. Example: more than the default page size: . POST . https://api.reliefweb.int/v2/countries?appname=REPLACE-WITH-APP-NAME . { "limit": 300 } . Example: skip the first 1000 sources (there are more than 1000, so normally also set limit): . POST . https://api.reliefweb.int/v2/sources?appname=REPLACE-WITH-APP-NAME . { "offset": 1000 } . Response links may include next/previous URLs for GET-style navigation. Rate limits are covered under Response limits. Next: Break down results .

183.title: Training
183.content: Submit a training opportunity for editorial review. The path segment is training (no trailing “s”). PUT|PATCH|DELETE https://api.reliefweb.int/v2/training/{uuid}?appname=REPLACE-WITH-APP-NAME . You need Access and credentials and Trusted URLs and UUIDs. For changes and withdrawals, see Update and Withdraw.

184.title: Field summary
184.content: Canonical schema: training.json. Field-by-field rules and examples: field reference. | Name | Required | Type | Description | . | url | yes | string (IRI / URL) | Immutable unique identifier in URL form under your trusted document prefix. Used to generate the training UUID. Does not need to resolve to a live page. Never change after first submission. | . | uuid | yes | string (UUID v5) | Training UUID v5 computed as `uuid5(ReliefWeb namespace, url)`. Must match what the server computes from the exact url string. | . | title | yes | string | Training title only. Do not put location, date, or organization name in this field. | . | source | yes | array of integer | Source organization ID(s) from /v2/sources (ReliefWeb integer taxonomy IDs, not UUIDs). | . | format | yes | array of integer | Training-format ID(s) from /v2/references/training-formats (on-site and/or online). On-site id is 4606; online is 4607. | . | country | conditional | array of integer | Country ID(s) from /v2/countries. Mandatory when format includes on-site; otherwise the property is not allowed. | . | dates | no | object | Training dates. Omit the whole object if the offering is ongoing or always available. When present, all three properties are required. | . | event_url | yes | string (IRI / URL) | Public page with more information about the opportunity. Do not use a social media URL here (you may mention social links in body). | . | cost | yes | string (enum) | Whether the training is free or fee-based. | . | fee_information | conditional | string | Exact course fee and what it does and does not cover (plain text). Cannot be replaced by a link alone. | . | category | yes | array of integer | Single training-type ID from /v2/references/training-types. | . | training_language | yes | array of integer | Language(s) in which the course or event is held, from /v2/references/languages. | . | professional_function | no | array of integer | Career-category ID(s) from /v2/references/career-categories. Tag only the most relevant (over-tagging reduces discoverability). | . | theme | no | array of integer | Single theme ID from /v2/references/themes. Choose only the most relevant. | . | language | yes | array of integer | Language(s) of this advertisement (English, Spanish, or French), from /v2/references/languages. This is the language of the ad text, not the course language. | . | body | yes | string (markdown or HTML) | Complete training description (introduction, methodology, objectives, audience). Do not replace with a link for further details. | . | how_to_register | yes | string (markdown or HTML) | Registration steps, conditions, and contact details. Do not replace with a bare link. If none required, say so explicitly (for example “No registration required.”). | . Taxonomy fields are integer ids — not UUIDs. Resolve them via the read API and /v2/references. Conditional fields . | Field | Rule | . | fee_information | Required when cost is fee-based; omit when cost is free. | . | country | Required when format includes on-site (4606); omit otherwise. | . | dates | If present, include start, end, and registration_deadline (ISO 8601). Omit the whole object for ongoing offerings. | . | Goal | See | . | Rules, examples, and lookups for each field | Training fields | . | Minimal and production-style payloads, troubleshooting | Training examples | . | Change some fields | Update | . | Withdraw | Withdraw | . Next: Training fields .

185.title: Update
185.content: Use PATCH to change some fields of an existing document. Send only the fields you want to change. Everything else stays as it is. The document must already exist, and the change is queued for processing and review like a new submission. To resend the whole document instead, see Replace. PATCH https://api.reliefweb.int/v2/{reports|jobs|training}/{uuid}?appname=REPLACE-WITH-APP-NAME . Send headers X-RW-POST-API-KEY and X-RW-POST-API-PROVIDER. See Access and credentials.

186.title: Change a field
186.content: Send the field with its new value. This example changes the title and body of a report and leaves every other field untouched: . curl -X PATCH "https://api.reliefweb.int/v2/reports/c27c51bd-e6b6-5c09-91fd-ef122afdde8e?appname=REPLACE-WITH-APP-NAME" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "X-RW-POST-API-KEY: YOUR-API-KEY" \ -H "X-RW-POST-API-PROVIDER: YOUR-PROVIDER-UUID" \ -d '{ "title": "Updated situation report for Country X", "body": "Revised executive summary." }' . Lists and objects . A field you send is set to exactly the value you send. For lists such as theme, country, or source, that means you send the complete new list, not only the item you want to add or remove. For example, if a report currently has "theme": [4587, 4595]: . | You send | The report ends up with | . | "theme": [4587, 4595, 4603] | Themes 4587, 4595, and 4603 (4603 added) | . | "theme": [4587] | Theme 4587 only (4595 removed) | . | "theme": [4603] | Theme 4603 only. Both existing themes are replaced. | . The same applies to objects such as image and training dates: send the whole object. Report attachments (file) are the exception. See Report attachments.

187.title: Clear an optional field
187.content: Set an optional field to null to remove its value: . { "origin": null } . Required fields cannot be cleared. A request such as { "title": null } fails with 400 and the message “Cannot clear mandatory field: title.” .

188.title: Report attachments
188.content: For reports, file works differently from other fields: attachments are merged by UUID, so you can add, remove, or reorder one attachment without resending the others. See Files and images.

189.title: Training: fields that depend on each other
189.content: Some training fields only make sense together. When your update touches one of them, the API checks the result against the values already stored on the document: . | fee_information is required when cost is fee-based, and must be empty otherwise. | country is required when format includes on-site training, and must be empty otherwise. | . For example, if a training is fee-based with a stored fee_information, switching it to free means changing both fields in the same request: . { "cost": "free", "fee_information": null } . Sending only "cost": "free" fails because the stored fee_information would no longer be allowed. See Conditional fields.

190.title: The url field
190.content: url is optional on PATCH because the path UUID already identifies the document. If you do send it, it must still match the UUID. See Trusted URLs and UUIDs.

191.title: Responses
191.content: . | Queued: 202 with “Document queued for processing.” | No changes: 200 with “No changes.” if the payload is identical to your previous submission. Nothing is queued again. | .

192.title: Errors
192.content: . | 400 if the payload is invalid, for example when clearing a required field. | 403 if the document was created by another provider. | 404 if no document exists for the UUID. | 422 if the document is refused, duplicate, or for reports archive. These documents can no longer be changed. | . See Responses, limits, and errors for all error codes and rate limits. Next: Withdraw .

193.title: Trusted URLs and UUIDs
193.content: When you request Publish access, you must provide trusted URL prefixes for your organization. The API only accepts document and media URLs that start with those approved prefixes. Those URLs also determine the UUIDs you send in every request.

194.title: Trusted URL prefixes
194.content: You configure three categories. Each category can list one or more prefixes: . | Category | Used for | . | Document prefixes | Document url (stable document identifier) | . | File prefixes | Attachment url (stable file identifier) and download_url | . | Image prefixes | Image download_url | . Use your organization’s own domain for permanent identifiers (url on documents and attachments). If ReliefWeb needs to download your files or images (download_url) from a separate CDN or storage host, add that host as an extra file or image prefix. Example for an organization that keeps permanent IDs on its own site and hosts PDF bytes on a CDN: . # Document prefixes (for document url) https://myorganization.org/report https://myorganization.org/job https://myorganization.org/training # File prefixes (organization domain for file.url + CDN for file.download_url) https://myorganization.org/files https://cdn.example.org/files # Image prefixes (for image.download_url) https://myorganization.org/images https://cdn.example.org/images . List every host and path prefix you will use. ReliefWeb configures the exact allowlist when it enables your provider.

195.title: Document URL (url)
195.content: The payload url is an immutable unique identifier in URL form: . | It must start with one of your trusted document prefixes | Prefer your organization’s own domain (for example https://myorganization.org/...) | It is used to generate the document UUID (see below) | It must never change after the first successful submission | It does not need to resolve to a live web page | . Examples: . https://myorganization.org/report/12345 https://myorganization.org/job/12345 https://myorganization.org/training/12345 .

196.title: Attachment URL vs download URL
196.content: ReliefWeb downloads attachments and images when it processes a submission. For report PDFs, two URL fields matter, and they play different roles. | Field | Role | . | url | Permanent attachment identifier. Used to generate the file UUID. Does not need to resolve. Never change it for that attachment. | . | download_url | Public URL where ReliefWeb downloads the file. Must start with one of your trusted file prefixes. You may change it when you publish a new version. | . Use your organization’s domain for url. Never use a variable CDN path, cloud storage URL, SharePoint link, or versioned filename as the permanent url. Those hosts change over time and would change the file UUID. Put them in download_url instead, and register the host in your trusted file prefixes. For images, send download_url only (plus checksum and metadata). See Files and images. Same host for identifier and download . When the PDF lives on your own site, url and download_url can be the same: . { "uuid": "78d63e84-e2b4-5467-813d-1c2456f40d63", "url": "https://myorganization.org/report/12345/attachment.pdf", "download_url": "https://myorganization.org/report/12345/attachment.pdf", "filename": "attachment.pdf", "checksum": "42fffa6c0e84ebab15f0f1ead8319efc448d0d883a0b492528997b4f17989755" } . Identifier on your domain, file on a CDN . When the bytes live on a CDN or external storage, keep url on your organization domain and put the CDN URL in download_url: . { "uuid": "78d63e84-e2b4-5467-813d-1c2456f40d63", "url": "https://myorganization.org/report/12345/attachment.pdf", "download_url": "https://cdn.example.org/files/2026-06/sitrep-v1.pdf", "filename": "attachment.pdf", "checksum": "42fffa6c0e84ebab15f0f1ead8319efc448d0d883a0b492528997b4f17989755" } . When you later publish sitrep-v2.pdf, keep the same url and uuid. Change only download_url and checksum: . { "uuid": "78d63e84-e2b4-5467-813d-1c2456f40d63", "url": "https://myorganization.org/report/12345/attachment.pdf", "download_url": "https://cdn.example.org/files/2026-06/sitrep-v2.pdf", "filename": "attachment.pdf", "checksum": "46e71dcadaee27ff9248490c5310bd2f9a04da602638b1f1d71bb01cdfaaf9a0" } . Avoid . Do not use the CDN or versioned path as the permanent identifier: . { "url": "https://cdn.example.org/files/2026-06/sitrep-v1.pdf", "download_url": "https://cdn.example.org/files/2026-06/sitrep-v1.pdf" } . That ties the file UUID to a path that will change when you upload sitrep-v2.pdf. Download URL rules . Download URLs must: . | Start with one of your trusted file or image prefixes | Be publicly reachable without login, a paywall, or signed access that expires before import | Match the schema rules: . | PDF filename: ends with lowercase .pdf (the download_url path has no extension requirement) | Image download_url: ends with .jpg, .png, or .webp | Size limits: PDF max 20MB; image min width 700px, max 5MB | . | . If ReliefWeb cannot download a file or image, processing fails even when the JSON validates. Checklist before you submit . | Document url starts with an approved document prefix on your organization domain | Every attachment url starts with an approved file prefix on your organization domain (permanent identifier, not a CDN or versioned path) | Every attachment download_url and image download_url starts with an approved file or image prefix and opens in a private browser window without signing in | PDF filename ends in .pdf; image download_url ends in .jpg, .png, or .webp; size limits match the schema | .

197.title: Document UUID
197.content: The Publish API uses UUID version 5. The server recomputes each UUID and rejects mismatches. You generate the document UUID (and each report file UUID). Cover images do not use a client-supplied UUID. uuid5(reliefweb_namespace, document_url) . | Namespace (fixed): 8e27a998-c362-5d1f-b152-d474e1d36af2 | Second argument: the document url exactly as it appears in your payload (character for character) | . | Document url | Document uuid | . | https://myorganization.org/report/12345 | c27c51bd-e6b6-5c09-91fd-ef122afdde8e | . | https://myorganization.org/job/12345 | efa7a5ff-a00c-500e-bc5d-d181874dc072 | . | https://myorganization.org/training/12345 | c2484d60-fa5d-591e-bcdd-401ffa63b92c | . Call /v2/{resource}/{document_uuid}. If uuid in the body does not match uuid5(reliefweb_namespace, document_url), the submission is rejected. Generating a document UUID . uuidgen (Linux) (the --name option is the url string): . uuidgen --sha1 --namespace 8e27a998-c362-5d1f-b152-d474e1d36af2 \ --name "https://myorganization.org/report/12345" . JavaScript (Node) (npm uuid): . import { v5 as uuidv5 } from 'uuid'; const NS = '8e27a998-c362-5d1f-b152-d474e1d36af2'; const url = 'https://myorganization.org/report/12345'; console.log(uuidv5(url, NS)); // c27c51bd-e6b6-5c09-91fd-ef122afdde8e . PHP (Symfony UID): . use Symfony\Component\Uid\Uuid; $ns = Uuid::fromString('8e27a998-c362-5d1f-b152-d474e1d36af2'); $url = 'https://myorganization.org/report/12345'; echo Uuid::v5($ns, $url)->toRfc4122(); . You can also use uuidtools v5.

198.title: File UUIDs (reports)
198.content: For PDF attachments, the document UUID is used as the namespace instead of the fixed ReliefWeb one: . uuid5(document_uuid, file_url) . | Namespace: the document uuid (see above) | Second argument: the attachment’s permanent url (not download_url) | . Using the report example above (document_uuid = c27c51bd-e6b6-5c09-91fd-ef122afdde8e): . | Attachment permanent url | File uuid (map key) | . | https://myorganization.org/report/12345/attachment.pdf | 78d63e84-e2b4-5467-813d-1c2456f40d63 | . That UUID is the key in the report file map, and the same value goes in the attachment’s uuid field (other fields abbreviated): . { "file": { "78d63e84-e2b4-5467-813d-1c2456f40d63": { "uuid": "78d63e84-e2b4-5467-813d-1c2456f40d63", "url": "https://myorganization.org/report/12345/attachment.pdf", "download_url": "…", "filename": "attachment.pdf", "checksum": "…" } } } . Keep it stable for the life of the attachment. Changing download_url does not change the file UUID. Generating a file UUID . JavaScript: . import { v5 as uuidv5 } from 'uuid'; const documentUuid = 'c27c51bd-e6b6-5c09-91fd-ef122afdde8e'; const fileUrl = 'https://myorganization.org/report/12345/attachment.pdf'; console.log(uuidv5(fileUrl, documentUuid)); // 78d63e84-e2b4-5467-813d-1c2456f40d63 . uuidgen: . uuidgen --sha1 --namespace c27c51bd-e6b6-5c09-91fd-ef122afdde8e \ --name "https://myorganization.org/report/12345/attachment.pdf" . Each file also requires a lowercase SHA-256 checksum of the file at download_url. See Files and images.

199.title: Images
199.content: Do not send a client uuid for image. ReliefWeb derives the media id from the checksum and download_url. Send download_url, checksum, description, and copyright.

200.title: Later submissions
200.content: . | Same document url produces the same document UUID. Use PUT or PATCH on that path. | Same attachment url produces the same file UUID. Change download_url and checksum to publish a new PDF version. | . Next: Create .

201.title: Withdraw
201.content: Use DELETE to unpublish an existing document. Unlike create and update, a withdrawal is applied immediately (nothing is queued), and the request has no body. DELETE https://api.reliefweb.int/v2/{reports|jobs|training}/{uuid}?appname=REPLACE-WITH-APP-NAME . Send headers X-RW-POST-API-KEY and X-RW-POST-API-PROVIDER. See Access and credentials. curl -X DELETE "https://api.reliefweb.int/v2/reports/c27c51bd-e6b6-5c09-91fd-ef122afdde8e?appname=REPLACE-WITH-APP-NAME" \ -H "X-RW-POST-API-KEY: YOUR-API-KEY" \ -H "X-RW-POST-API-PROVIDER: YOUR-PROVIDER-UUID" .

202.title: Responses
202.content: Withdrawal returns 200 (not 202, since nothing is queued). | Withdrawn: 200 with “Document withdrawn.” The document status is now withdrawn. | Already withdrawn: 200 with “Document already withdrawn.” Nothing changes, so it is safe to retry. | Refused, duplicate, or archived: 200 with a message such as “Document is already publicly unavailable (marked as refused).” The document is not changed and keeps its current status. Reports can also be archive. | .

203.title: Errors
203.content: . | 403 if the document was created by another provider. | 404 if no document exists for the UUID. See Responses, limits, and errors for all error codes and rate limits. | .

204.title: Expired jobs and training
204.content: ReliefWeb marks jobs and training as expired automatically after they close. You can still withdraw an expired document, and its status then becomes withdrawn.

205.title: Reopen a withdrawn document
205.content: To reopen a withdrawn document (or an expired job or training), submit it again with PUT or PATCH. The submission is handled like any other and goes through the normal review process again. See Replace and Update. Next: Responses, limits, and errors .
